gap: Novice routes to evaluation and intervention
discriminating_question: Does successful novice practice require personal code understanding or can evaluation be distributed to tools and other people?
opposing_expected_observations: Independent novice correction would challenge an expertise prerequisite; inability to assess outputs or unreleased demos would bound the claim.

discriminating_question: Do disciplined prompting and self-correction explain recovery when the necessary interface is unavailable?
opposing_expected_observations: A failure-to-success transition only after API availability supports an external condition; recovery without such change would favor user workflow.

discriminating_question: Can expert builders resolve failures through adjustments, or does a model capability change determine viability?
opposing_expected_observations: Reported shelving then restart after model improvement challenges a purely local user-skill account; successful adjustment before it would favor that account.

gap: Expert failure, shutdown and expanding user demands
discriminating_question: Does iterative repair preserve useful delegation, or can repairs cease to make the workflow workable?
opposing_expected_observations: A reported shutdown despite expertise challenges indefinite revision as a sufficient mechanism; bounded recalibration after scope expansion shows an alternative response.

gap: Expert limits and deliberately restricted use
discriminating_question: Does expertise sustain wider delegation, or does supervision load and uncertainty make restriction rational?
opposing_expected_observations: Experienced restriction or overload would challenge monotonic expansion; sustained unattended success would challenge attention as the limiting condition.

discriminating_question: Can output correctness suffice, or do reviewers/users renegotiate what counts as useful?
opposing_expected_observations: A concrete shift from factual correctness to appropriateness supports criteria revision; settled criteria reliably predicting actual value would challenge it.

discriminating_question: Can workers recover and revise work when manual implementation is deliberately unavailable?
opposing_expected_observations: Successful changes through documentation or environment would challenge takeover as a necessary route; inability to alter consequential failures would bound that alternative.

discriminating_question: Is intervention capacity located in the individual or in organizational relationships and vendor access?
opposing_expected_observations: Reported recovery requiring exceptional provider access supports distributed repair capacity; the same resolution readily available to ordinary users would weaken this condition.
